In [[topology]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''James reduced product''' or '''James construction''' ''J''(''X'') of a [[topological space]] ''X'' with given basepoint ''e'' is the [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient]] of the [[disjoint union]] of all powers ''X'', ''X''<sup>2</sup>, ''X''<sup>3</sup>, ... obtained by identifying points (''x''<sub>1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''k''&minus;1</sub>,''e'',''x''<sub>''k''+1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''n''</sub>) with (''x''<sub>1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''k''&minus;1</sub>, ''x''<sub>''k''+1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''n''</sub>). In other words, its underlying set is the free monoid generated by ''X'' (with unit ''e''). It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Ioan|last=James|authorlink=Ioan James|year=1955}}.

For a connected [[CW complex]] ''X'', the James reduced product ''J''(''X'') has the same homotopy type as ΩΣ''X'', the [[loop space]] of the [[Suspension (topology)|suspension]] of ''X''.

The commutative analogue of the James reduced product is called the [[infinite symmetric product]].
